text: British doctor Rahmeh Aladwan circulates posts excusing synagogue attacks and shares an image branding Chief Rabbi Ephraim Mirvis “Rabbi Genocide” immediately after Jews are killed in Manchester.

An Israeli mother in Ireland says her doctor lectured her about “genocide” while she was about to give birth during a high-risk pregnancy. She told the doctor the comments were inappropriate and refused further care from her.
A street poster declares that a ceasefire does not matter and “We don’t stop until Israel ceases to exist.”

Five Jewish members sued Brooklyn's Park Slope Food Coop, alleging an intimidation campaign over its Israel boycott: they were called “racist,” “genocide supporter” and “spiritually disfigured.” In the boycott organizers' Signal chat, one activist wrote “Long live Yahya Al-Sinwar.”
Antizionists at a Los Angeles anti-ICE protest display support for Hamas and call for death to Israeli soldiers, linking their American activism to jihadist violence.
A Palestinian woman interviewed in Canada says she supports Hamas, calls its members the true fighters for Palestine and adds “alhamdulillah.”

At Seattle’s No Kings march, a protester shouts “Long live October 7” and tells journalist Brandi Kruse that the massacre’s rapes and murders were Israeli propaganda. So Oct. 7 was a great day, but also it never happened and was Israeli propaganda.
Canadian antizionist Firas al Najim leads chants that “October 7 was justified,” with a child beside him joining the demonstration.
A Bergen, Norway rally poster urges “Support Palestinian resistance” and celebrates one year of “Al-Aqsa Flood,” Hamas’s name for the October 7 massacre.
An antizionist crowd boos Reggio Emilia mayor Marco Massari and shouts “shame” when he calls for the release of Israeli hostages while honoring UN rapporteur Francesca Albanese.
An antizionist woman spits at an Israeli’s car window in New York, screams abuse and declares, “I love Hamas.”
Antisemitic graffiti brands Mexico’s Jewish president Claudia Sheinbaum a “Jewish whore” and crosses out a Star of David; Her leftist politics and criticism of Israel offer no protection.

Good Morning Britain presenter Kate Garraway says the Manchester synagogue attacker’s religion and motive are unknown, despite being a Syrian named Jihad. The Tweets on the right are images from the attack, being blocked by Twitter's embed tool. Click through to see (WARNING: GRAPHIC).

NYC - Mental health provider Jennifer Koonings filmed herself shouting antisemitic slurs - 'baby killers' and 'fuck Israel' - at Jewish individuals peacefully going about their day. This isn’t a lapse in judgment. It raises serious concerns about her fitness to treat patients, especially Jewish clients. She's affiliated with Inspire Mental Health Services.
Yuen Lee, an assurance manager at KPMG. Earlier today, she was filmed calling a Jewish man a “Zionist pig” at Chelsea Piers Flatiron. Imagine being one of her Jewish colleagues at @KPMG.

FBI agents in Pennsylvania foiled an alleged plot to attack synagogues and other Jewish institutions on the eve of Yom Kippur, prompting increased security in Pittsburgh’s Jewish community. Federal agents arrested 21 year old U.S. citizen Jonathan Kramer at a hotel in Cranberry Township, where authorities say he was found with a rifle, dozens of knives and around 200 rounds of ammunition. According to court documents, Kramer had expressed support for ISIS and allegedly planned mass casualty attacks at several locations, as well as poisoning food at synagogues across the state.

A 12-year-old Jewish girl at Etiwanda Intermediate School (California) was walking in a hallway when another student started beating her with a stick. Staff told the attacker to stop — then walked away. The girl was then pinned against a table and choked. She was told to “shut her stupid Jewish ass up.” Then come the Nazi salutes in the hallways. Swastikas on school property and on the textbooks on her desk. Hitler jokes. Holocaust taunts. Harassment about missing school for a Jewish holiday.
On Yom Kippur, a synagogue in Beville, Ontario is under attack. Shots fired at the Sons of Jacob synagogue, bullets piecing windows. A police officer shot.
A group of ppl attacked a jewish group on the streets of @NYCMayor the jihadist city. One man looks like he is holding a table to hit them.  One man kicks a female in the head.
A swastika was found carved into a window at the Inwood LIRR station in Lawrence, New York. Mayor Samuel Nahmias condemned it and announced a police investigation.

In Crown Heights, Brooklyn, a man chased a visibly Jewish yeshiva student while brandishing a knife and shouting “Heil f---ing Hitler,” followed him to the door, said “Now I know where you live,” and appeared to slash bike tires. Police charged Bronx resident Devin Best with aggravated harassment as a hate crime and menacing.
Frum TikTok shares a video of someone invading a Jewish space and harassing Jews at a Chabad center in Virginia.

Zohran Mamdani’s pledge to keep Jewish New Yorkers safe is contrasted with a report about a city health staffer in Mamdani's administration wishing Israelis were wiped out and Claire’s post connecting the staffer to an older taunt aimed at a hostage’s mother.

Spike Lee wore Palestinian symbols during NBA All-Star weekend, when Deni Avdija made his debut as the first Israeli All-Star. Hen Mazzig criticizes the display as intruding on Avdija’s achievement; The Persian Jewess explicitly alleges Lee wore the flag to harass him. Emily Austin challenges Lee’s claim that he did not know who Avdija was.
Two men are convicted of plotting an ISIS-inspired mass shooting against Jews in Manchester, England, United Kingdom; a third is convicted of failing to disclose the plot.
A Jewish customer reports finding a “Free Palestine” note inside Hanukkah pajamas ordered from Bloomingdale’s

Congress investigates allegations that the American Psychological Association tolerated antisemitism, including events that attacked Zionism and Jewish members while receiving continuing-education credit.
A video presented as recorded at Washington’s Union Station shows hostility directed at Jews.
Montreal antizionist Mahmoud Khalil verbally abuses Israel supporters.
Students dressed like Hamas members disrupt October 7 survivor Yoni’s account at Pomona College, confronting a survivor of the attack on Kibbutz Mefalsim.
Students from Escuela Humanos in Buenos Aires chant “Today we will burn the Jews” on their graduation-trip bus while an adult dances with them. The school’s motto is “Building more humane people.”
Agitators in London chant “Khaybar, Khaybar, ya Yahud”—invoking the historic Muslim battle against Jews—and say Muhammad’s army will return.

Actor Javier Bardem wears a keffiyeh at the Emmy Awards, calls Gaza a genocide, endorses the boycott of Israeli film institutions, and urges commercial and diplomatic pressure and sanctions on Israel.
A crowd member immediately shouts “Free Palestine” when comedian Big Jay Oakerson says he is Jewish on stage.
George Mason University reinstated its Students for Justice in Palestine chapter after a police investigation uncovered guns, ammunition and signs reading “death 2 Jews” at the former leaders’ home.

After a child asks a shop for a Palestinian flag and is offered an Israeli one, his father returns to berate the shopkeeper: “Why would you tell him you have the Jewish flag?” followed by “Fuck Israel” and “Go fuck yourself.”

WNBA player Natasha Cloud tells followers to cross-reference AIPAC with the Epstein files and calls Zionism no different from the KKK. An earlier screenshot shows her describing Israel’s founding as white settlers seizing land, raping women and murdering men and children.

Undercover reporter Zach Sage Fox discusses antizionist hostility in London and the threat it poses to Jewish life, drawing a warning for New York under Zohran Mamdani. "Where will the Jews go if we make Israel Palestine?" "They can go to hell!"
